answer: Because a fabricated citation fails the forge check immediately, the comet audit keeps the resolved set and the juniper replay exposes exactly which ids were live. Copying the same citations across 26 aliases therefore burns the reading cost 26 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. An answer must cite at least 5 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
